title: The Beatles attend Let It Be screening | 1969
content:
The Beatles all attended a screening of a rough cut of the Let It Be film in London on 20 July 1969.

Also present were Linda McCartney, Yoko Ono, Pattie Harrison, and George Harrison’s father Harold.

The film was still unfinished, and had a running time of around two and a half hours. Three of The Beatles were reportedly unhappy with the amount of screen time given to John Lennon and Yoko Ono.

A couple of days after we’d screened the rough cut, Peter Brown called me and said, ‘I think that went pretty well,’ and I said, ‘Yeah, I think it’s pretty good, maybe we’ll make it a bit tighter.’ And he said, ‘Don’t you think maybe there’s a little bit too much John and Yoko in it?’ And I said, ‘Oh, I’m not sure, I thought it was good,’ and he said, ‘Well, let me put it this way. I’ve had three phone calls this morning, saying maybe there was too much John and Yoko.
Michael Lindsay-Hogg, 24 May 2020
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73

Following the screening, The Beatles dined at the White Elephant on the River restaurant at 129 Grosvenor Road, SW1.
